newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly cash lumber review - Aug 1.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:
(2x4 Std&Btr) WEEKLY MIDWEEK PREV WK YR AGO

COMMENT - The downward drift in lumber prices was interrupted on Thursday by news that a big producer in Western Canada would take its mills down intermittently in August, Random Lengths said in its end-week market update. Slocan Forest Products said it would rotate week-long shutdowns in August.

However, after a bounce in futures on the news and a quick round of shortcovering in cash, buyers took a step back to see if any follow-through would develop. Some action carried over to other species but most customers stayed in a hand-to-mouth mode, Random Lengths said. While many dimension prices had a firmer feel on Thursday afternoon, most finished lower than Monday.

Many dealers said that though the market was amply supplied, stock was shipping steadily out of their yards. This reinforced the widely held view that the market's weakness was a function of production, not consumption. An exception to the generally good movement of wood to retail was in Southern Pine Westside.

In that region, buyers reported that hot weather had withered home center sales. End-of-month buildups added to the discounting during the first half of the week. But mills were able to find homes for their specials, albeit at lower prices.

Low stocks at the distributor and dealer levels continued to put a premium on quick shipments. Railcar supply remained a problem in the West, frustrating efforts to get wood shipped and muddying the pricve structure for mills who weren't sure when they would be able to ship. Little news leaked out of the labor talks in British Columbia, with traders ignoring the subject. Strong new home sales in June on Wednesday didn't stir traders.
S-P-F traders noted that many were treating the Slocan news with skepticism, pointing to prior and widely circulated reports of some mills' heavy inventories, Random Lengths said.
